name: Beng
catalog_citation: Paperno, Denis. 2014. Grammatical sketch of Beng: Beng phonology. Mandenkan 51. OpenEdition, journals.openedition.org/mandenkan/557 (HTML full text + 4-pp. PDF).
catalog_locator: Ch. 'Beng phonology', sec. 4.1.1 Tones (paras 11-12), 4.1.2 Syllable structure (para 19), 4.1.4 Tonal sandhi (para 24)
catalog_quote: Beng has three tone levels, including low (marked L or with the grave diacritic: v̀), mid (marked M or with the macron sign: v̄), and high (H or the acute sign: v́). There are minimal triples distinguished just by tone levels, e.g. báŋ́ ‘trap’ – bāŋ̄ ‘rope’ – bàŋ̀ ‘shoulder’; pɛ́ŋ́ ‘mortar’– pɛ̄ŋ̄ ‘tale’ – pɛ̀ŋ̀ ‘debt’. In accordance with their names, realization of the tones is manifested primarily in the pitch of the syllable. Pitch, however, also shows some contextual effects, including those of phrasal position. ... In addition to level tones, Beng possesses four countour tones: HL (v̂), ML (v), LH (v̌), MH (v̈). ... Beng’s main prosodic unit is the syllable, which sometimes corresponds historically to a disyllabic foot of other South Mande languages as a result of a syncope CVLV>CLV. ... Any of those components can be absent, as long as the syllable has one tone bearing element, i…

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Deciding quotation confirmed verbatim in the held OpenEdition HTML/PDF of Paperno 2014 sec. 4 at the cited paragraphs (11-12, 16, 19). (2) The classification 'tonal, no word stress described' rests on a 2014 130-pp fieldwork grammar sketch, the best available description per Glottolog and web search (no reference grammar, no instrumental prosody study, no JIPA illustration exists for Beng). (3) downloaded now and Paesler 1992 Esquisse phonologique (Rosetta/archive.org) — three level tones + four contour tones, syllable as tone-placement unit, no accent; the full Mandenkan 51 PDF — whole-volume a full-text search for stress/accent finds no Beng stress/accent statement; Paesler 1989 JWAL (scanned) — lexical tonal verb classes and a question floating L tone, no stress. All three confirm the classification. (4) Nothing suggests a reclassify; only a low-priority dictionary

sources.citation: Paesler, Wolfgang. 1992. Esquisse phonologique du beng, parler de Ouassadougou (S.-P. de M'Bahiakro, Côte d'Ivoire). In: Esquisses phonologiques de trois langues ivoriennes: beng, dida, yaouré. Abidjan: ILA / Paris: ACCT. (Rosetta Project scan, archive.org rosettaproject_nhb_phon-1, 34 images, 300 ppi, ABBYY text layer)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: 'En beng, il existe trois niveaux tonals. Sur des mots monosyllabiques on trouve trois tons ponctuels [H], [M], [B] et quatre tons modulés ... deux sont montants [MH], [BH], et deux sont descendants [HB], [MB].' ... 'Cela montre que la syllabe est l'unité de placement des tons.' All nine H/M/B combinations attested on CV.CV disyllables (Tableau 12). No mention of accent or stress anywhere in the scanned text (a full-text search for stress/accent/stress: 0 hits). Note: scan may be partial (34 images of a work cited as 50 pp; tone chapter is announced as 'simplement une introduction').

sources.citation: Paesler, Wolfgang. 1989. How to distinguish statement and question in Beng. Journal of West African Languages 19(1): 57-74. (open PDF from journalofwestafricanlanguages.org, image-only; scanned at 300 dpi, one tesseract)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: Analyses Beng verbs by lexical tonal classes (H/M/L patterns on root + infinitival suffix) and derives question forms by adding a floating L tone at the right edge of the tonal tier. No mention of stress or accent (scanned a full-text search for stress/accent found nothing). Treats Beng prosody as purely tonal.
